messages.content: I'm planning a camping trip and I need to know the weather forecast. Can you fetch me the weather data for the campsite located at latitude 35. and longitude for the next 10 days including daily temperature and precipitation forecasts? Also, I prefer the temperature 2 minute max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches. Don't give me hourly information

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants weather forecast for next 10 days, daily temperature and precipitation forecasts. They want temperature 2m max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches. They don't want hourly info.

We have a tool `requests_get` that can call Open-Meteo API. We need to construct a GET request to the Open-Meteo API endpoint. The user gave latitude 35. and longitude ??? The user says "latitude 35. and longitude for the next 10 days". It seems they omitted the longitude. Possibly they want us to ask for missing longitude? But we can guess maybe they want a generic location? The user didn't provide a specific longitude. So we might need to ask them for the longitude. Or we could interpret "latitude 35." as incomplete. The user also said "Don't give me hourly information".

We can use the Open-Meteo API. The typical endpoint is https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast. We need to pass query parameters: latitude, longitude, daily=temperature_2m_max, precipitation_sum, timezone, start_date, end_date, etc. We need to convert units: temperature in Fahrenheit, precipitation in inches. The API supports units: temperature_unit=fahrenheit, precipitation_unit=inches. We need daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum. We need to set start_date to today, end_date to 10 days from now. We need to set timezone to local or UTC. We need to set daily=... and exclude hourly. The API will return daily data only if we specify daily param. We can also set "hourly" param to none. But we can just not include hourly param.

We need to get today's date. Let's compute start_date = current date. End_date = start_date + 9 days? Actually next 10 days inclusive? Usually we want 10 days including today. So end_date = start_date + 9 days. We'll compute that.

We need to ask for missing longitude. The user didn't provide it. So we need to ask them for the longitude. Alternatively, we can ask them to confirm the location. The user said "latitude 35. and longitude for the next 10 days". That is ambiguous. We can respond asking for the longitude. Then we can proceed.

Thus we should ask: "Could you please provide the longitude?"
